# Atomdown

> Atomdown adds persistent block IDs, groups, and extensible metadata to Markdown. Documents remain valid CommonMark for people, tools, and AI agents.

Use Atomdown for block references, review workflows, and application-defined block metadata. Visible Markdown remains the source of truth.

Core syntax:

```markdown
<!-- <atomdown version="1"/> -->
<!-- <atom id="4P8W2H6K" slug="claim"/> -->
<!-- <atom-group id="7K3M9X2D" slug="findings"> -->
<!-- </atom-group> -->
```

Editing rules:

1. Preserve Atomdown comments and unknown attributes.
2. Apply an atom marker to the next top-level Markdown block.
3. Keep each directive on its own source line.
4. Preserve an ID when you move its item.
5. Generate a new ID when you copy an item.
6. Keep group markers balanced. Atomdown Core 1 does not permit nested groups.
7. Run `atomdown lint FILE` after you edit a document.

## Standard

- [Atomdown Core 1](SPEC.md): Normative syntax, identity, extension, and conformance rules.
- [XML schema](schema/atomdown-1.xsd): XSD 1.0 model for normalized metadata.
- [Conformance corpus](testdata/README.md): Valid, mixed, malformed, and golden documents.

## Implementation

- [Project guide](README.md): Design, CLI commands, and Go library examples.
- [Parser](parser.go): CommonMark and Atomdown parsing.
- [Token API](token.go): Lossless Markdown, directive, and whitespace tokens.
- [Extension API](processor.go): Transform hooks for embedded applications.

Machine-readable commands:

```text
atomdown parse FILE
atomdown tokens FILE
atomdown lint --json FILE
atomdown xml FILE
atomdown strip FILE
atomdown id
```
